theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorLayout.meets {pMain pDivide n g free : ℕ} {μ : ℕ → ℤ}
    (hmain : P[pMain]?=some (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorLayout.body pDivide)) (hdiv : P[pDivide]?=some _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightSmallDivide.body)
    (hw : (lim.space : ℤ) ≤ lim.word) (hn : 0 < n) (hg : 0 < g)
    (hspace : _root_.ThreeSum.EncodedColorLayout.normalizedEnd free n g+1 ≤ lim.space)
    (hword : (_root_.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorLayout.word n g : ℤ) ≤ lim.word) (hd : d < lim.depth) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Meets lim P pMain d [n,g,free] μ (_root_.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorLayout.time n g)
      (fun r ν => r=(_root_.ThreeSum.EncodedColorLayout.normalizedEnd free n g : ℤ) ∧ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Seg ν free (_root_.ThreeSum.EncodedColorLayout.normalizedHeads free n g) ∧ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Kept μ ν free) := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let positive $n,g$ be input length and band size, $a$ an arbitrary free address, and $\lambda,P,d,\mu$ limits, program, depth and memory. Suppose the program contains the layout and division bodies, addresses fit words, the computed normalized-end address plus one fits memory, the stated layout word bound fits, and a nested call is allowed. The layout call writes its normalized-header values at $a$, returns

$$\operatorname{normalizedEnd}(a,n,g),$$

runs within its specified budget and preserves every cell below $a$.

This computes the physical color-normalization buffers from original size and band size.
